transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess what finally made me come in is… over these last months, my head just won’t stay on one thing. I drive for work and do sales-type deliveries, and normally I’m pretty solid with details — notes, callbacks, who asked for what, that kind of thing. But lately my mind jumps at everything. A CB chirp, a fuel price sign, even just some new idea that pops into my head, and suddenly I’ve lost the thread.

I’ll be meaning to check a client’s delivery note, and then something catches my attention and I miss something I normally wouldn’t. Or I tell somebody I’ll call them back, and then my brain’s already on three other things and I forget who it was. It’s embarrassing, honestly, because I’ve been doing this kind of work a long time and I don’t usually make those little mistakes. So… yeah, that’s what got me worried enough to come in.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

I don’t know that I’d say “down” exactly. I mean, I get frustrated with myself, sure, because I’m messing up little things I usually keep straight, and that wears on you after a while. But sad like I can’t enjoy anything, or like everything feels empty… no, I haven’t really noticed that.

As far as losing interest, I don’t think so. If anything, I still want to do things, I just get irritated when I can’t keep my focus where it’s supposed to be. So… no, I wouldn’t say sadness or not caring about things is the main issue for me.
Do you often feel restless, as if you need to be doing something all the time, or find yourself acting without thinking things through?

Yeah… restless is a good word for it. I don’t know if I’d say I’m doing anything crazy without thinking, but I definitely feel like I need to be doing something, like I can’t just sit and leave things alone.

Like with work, I’ll get home and instead of being done with the day, I’ll start rewriting my route plans, going back over them, thinking, “Well, if I move this stop here and call that guy earlier, maybe I can shave off time.” And then I’ll think of some new driver who might need checking on, so I’ll send a message or make a call after hours when it probably could’ve waited. It feels important in the moment, like I’m being helpful or getting ahead, but sometimes I step back and think, why am I still working on this?

Same thing at home. I’ll notice something small, like a loose handle or a thing in the garage that’s not where I want it, and suddenly I’m fixing it or reorganizing stuff. If I sit on the couch too long, I get this antsy feeling, like I’m wasting time or like I should be up handling something. It’s not even always something that needs doing right then. I just… I keep making jobs for myself.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing faster than usual?

Yeah, the sleep part, definitely. That’s actually one of the weirder things, because I’ve never been someone who did great on no sleep, you know? But lately most nights I’ll sleep maybe three or four hours, and then I’m just… up. Like before daylight, wide awake, and I don’t feel worn out the way I’d expect.

I’ll look at the clock and think, “That can’t be enough,” but my body’s already acting like it’s time to start the day. I’m not dragging myself out of bed or hitting snooze over and over. I’m just ready to roll, like I already had a full night. It doesn’t really make sense to me, because three or four hours used to catch up with me fast, but now I wake up and feel like I should get moving.
Have you had any periods where your mood was unusually high, overly confident, or irritable, along with a surge of energy or an urge to keep doing more and more things at once?

Yeah… I think that’s probably closer to what’s been going on. It’s not like I’m walking around happy-go-lucky all day, but for months now I’ve had these stretches where I’m just really fired up, like everything is going to work out, like I can handle whatever comes up and I should just keep pushing. I’ll get this feeling like, “No, I’ve got this, I can get all of it done,” even when maybe I’m taking on too much.

And then the other side of it is I get irritated way too easy. Little things at home or out in the yard will set me off more than they should. Something’s not where I left it, or a job isn’t going the way I pictured it, and I’ll snap or get sharp about it. That’s not really how I think of myself normally. I mean, I can get annoyed like anybody, but this feels quicker, like I’m already wound up and it doesn’t take much.

So yeah, it’s kind of both — either I’m overly revved up and confident that I can keep doing more and more, or I’m touchy and snapping over small stuff. And it’s been going on long enough now that I can’t really brush it off as just a bad day.
